content: Venice treacle, also known as Andromachi theriaca, Theriacum Andromachi, or treacle of Andromachus, was a medicinal preparation in pharmacy that was honeyor molasses-based and believed to have antidotal properties against venom. It was originally developed in Italy and later exported across Europe, particularly from Venice. The formulation of this theriac, as recorded in the 1686 Amsterdam Pharmacopoeia, included a wide variety of ingredients, many of which were translated from their old Latin names into modern Latin nomenclature where possible. However, not all ingredients are fully identified. Roots: Iris Balsamorhiza deltoidea Potentilla reptans (creeping cinquefoil) Rheum rhabarbarum (garden rhubarb) Zingiber (ginger) Angustafolia odorata Gentiana (gentian) Meum athamanticum (spignel) Valeriana (valerian) Corydalis cava (hollowroot) Agaricus (a type of fungus) Cinnamomum zeylanicum (cinnamon) Cinnamomum aromaticum (cassia) Leaves: Teucrium scordium (water germander) Fraxinus excelsior (ash tree) Clinopodium calamintha (lesser calamint) Marrubium vulgare (white or common horehound) Cymbopogon citratus (West-Indian lemongrass) Teucrium chamaedrys (wall germander) Cupressus (cypress) Laurus nobilis (bay laurel) Polium montanum Piper nigrum (black pepper) Piper longum (long pepper) Juniperus (juniper) Syzygium aromaticum (clove) Flowers: Rosa (rose) Crocus sativus (saffron) Lavandula stoechas (French lavender) Centaurea minoris Seeds: Brassica napus (rapeseed) Petroselinum (parsley) Nigella sativa (black cumin) Pimpinella anisum (anise) Elettaria cardamomum (cardamom) Foeniculum vulgare (fennel) Hypericum perforatum (St. John’s wort) Seseli Thlaspi Daucus carota (carrot) Lavandula angustifolia (common or English lavender) Papaver somniferum (opium poppy) Glycyrrhiza (licorice) Cytinus hypocistis Acaciae (acacia) Styrax benzoin (benzoin resin) Gummi arabicum (gum arabic) Sagapeni (a wax from an unidentified tree, likely a species of Ferula) Gummi Opopanax chironium Gummi Ferula foetida Dead Sea bitumen Commiphora (a tree producing myrrh) Incense Turpentine from Cyprus Boli armen (Armenian bole, a type of clay) This complex mixture of botanical, resinous, and mineral ingredients reflects the historical pharmacological practices of the time, where such multi-ingredient formulations were believed to have broad therapeutic effects, particularly as antidotes to poisons and venoms.
